paths.description: Homepage portal archetype and primary search entry; tested desktop, 360px, dark, reduced-motion, high-contrast, network, performance, accessibility and memory conditions.
Primary search completion and result-list archetype.
App-like route-planning form archetype including empty submission.
Authentication entry inspected for labels, autocomplete and WebAuthn/passkey support.

findings.summary: The portal ignores the operating system dark theme.
findings.evidence: Desktop screenshots under light and prefers-color-scheme: dark are pixel-identical in surface treatment; the rendered CSS declares color-scheme: light.
findings.suggestedFix: Declare color-scheme: light dark and map surface/text tokens through prefers-color-scheme or light-dark(), including the consent layer.

findings.summary: Primary state changes do not use View Transitions.
findings.evidence: The platform probe found no view-transition CSS while the portal has tab, menu and content state changes.
findings.suggestedFix: Use document.startViewTransition() for meaningful same-document state changes, with a reduced-motion fallback.

findings.summary: The consent prompt obscures primary content on every fresh load.
findings.evidence: Desktop and 360px screenshots show a fixed consent sheet covering the lower viewport before interaction; on mobile it hides the lead story.
findings.suggestedFix: Replace the load-time obstruction with a compact, dismissible choice surface and keep the core portal usable while a decision is pending.

findings.summary: The consent surface is custom chrome without dialog semantics.
findings.evidence: The homepage overlay was absent from dialog/[role=dialog]/aria-modal probes, while the settings DOM uses a custom .szn-cmp-dialog-container.
findings.suggestedFix: Implement the modal choice with <dialog>, a labelled heading, focus containment, Escape/cancel handling and an explicit close path.

findings.summary: Search results force a desktop-width layout on mobile.
findings.evidence: At 360x800 the search result layout reported scrollWidth 1232px, clientWidth 360px and 872px horizontal overflow.
findings.suggestedFix: Make result containers intrinsically sized (max-inline-size:100%), reflow tabs/cards at narrow widths, and test at 320-400 CSS px.

findings.summary: Keyboard focus is invisible on many primary controls and targets are undersized.
findings.evidence: The focus probe found none/0px outlines on search tabs, submit buttons and article links; many controls are 28-32px high. Lighthouse also failed target-size.
findings.suggestedFix: Apply a high-contrast :focus-visible indicator and provide at least 44x44 CSS-pixel touch targets without removing native focus.

findings.summary: Cold-load performance is far outside the good range.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse measured LCP 10.6s, FCP 8.6s, TBT 800ms and performance 33; the trace independently measured LCP 4.13s and TBT 302ms.
findings.suggestedFix: Prioritise the LCP resource, defer below-fold portal modules, and split/schedule non-critical JavaScript.

findings.summary: Late content and unsized images shift the mobile page.
findings.evidence: The 360px layout observer measured CLS 0.125 with a 0.096 shift around 6.9s; all 100 inspected images lacked width/height attributes.
findings.suggestedFix: Reserve image/ad/widget space with width/height or aspect-ratio and stabilise late-loading modules.

findings.summary: Heavy scripting repeatedly blocks the main thread.
findings.evidence: The trace recorded six long tasks (longest 163ms, TBT 302ms); mobile layout recorded tasks up to 206ms and Lighthouse TBT was 800ms.
findings.suggestedFix: Break work into scheduler.yield()/postTask chunks, delay non-critical widgets, and move suitable processing off-thread.

findings.summary: Resource delivery is excessively heavy and redirect-rich.
findings.evidence: HAR captured 480 requests and 16.7MB transferred, including 315 images/14.2MB and six redirects; many preview images lacked cache headers.
findings.suggestedFix: Remove redirect loops, lazy-load below-fold modules, use responsive image variants and durable cache headers, and audit LCP priority.

findings.summary: Non-critical and third-party code dominates initial load.
findings.evidence: HAR recorded 452 third-party-origin requests and a 644KB client bundle plus 406KB assistant widget and 153KB tag manager; Lighthouse reported TTI 65.6s.
findings.suggestedFix: Code-split portal widgets, conditionally import the assistant and analytics, and remove duplicated/unused client code.

findings.summary: Many images and controls lack accessible names.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse failed button-name, image-alt, link-name and frame-title; the image probe counted 61/100 images without alt, and DOM probes found unnamed buttons/links.
findings.suggestedFix: Give every actionable control and iframe an accessible name; use meaningful alt text or alt="" for decorative images.

findings.summary: Text and essential UI fail minimum colour contrast.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse accessibility scored 70 and failed the color-contrast audit on the rendered homepage.
findings.suggestedFix: Adjust text, icon and state tokens to WCAG AA ratios in every theme and verify normal, high-contrast and forced-colors modes.

findings.summary: Heading structure and focus treatment do not provide a reliable reading/keyboard path.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse failed heading-order; the DOM begins with empty H1s then H6 before H2, and the focus probe found invisible focus on most tested links/buttons.
findings.suggestedFix: Use one descriptive H1, sequential section headings, labelled landmarks and a consistent visible focus ring.

findings.summary: Reflow and target-size support fail on a primary path.
findings.evidence: Search results overflow by 872px at 360px and Lighthouse failed target-size; the homepage also includes videos with no <track> elements.
findings.suggestedFix: Fix narrow-screen reflow, enlarge targets, and provide captions/transcripts for editorial media that conveys information.

findings.summary: The homepage emits runtime/network errors.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse failed errors-in-console; HAR recorded aborted fetches and a 400 autologin request.
findings.suggestedFix: Remove avoidable failed requests, handle expected aborts without console errors, and add regression monitoring for uncaught/runtime failures.

findings.summary: Image sizing and aspect-ratio hygiene is poor.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse failed image-aspect-ratio and image-size-responsive; 100/100 inspected images omitted dimensions and 30 were oversized.
findings.suggestedFix: Emit intrinsic width/height, correct aspect ratios and srcset/sizes for each image slot.

findings.summary: Deprecated APIs, source-map defects and BFCache blockers remain.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse reported one deprecation, invalid source maps, inspector issues and four BFCache failure reasons.
findings.suggestedFix: Resolve deprecations and inspector issues, publish valid source maps, and remove unload/runtime patterns that block BFCache.

findings.summary: The CSP is only a frame policy and key response defenses are missing.
findings.evidence: Headers show CSP only frame-ancestors, with no script/style/default-src policy; X-Content-Type-Options, Referrer-Policy and Permissions-Policy are absent. HTTPS and HSTS are present.
findings.suggestedFix: Deploy a nonce/hash-based CSP with default/script/style/object/base directives plus nosniff, strict Referrer-Policy and a least-privilege Permissions-Policy.

findings.summary: The fresh homepage has a very large analytics and third-party footprint.
findings.evidence: Tracker capture saw 36 third-party origins including Google Tag Manager/Analytics; HAR attributed 452 requests and 16.45MB to non-main origins, before consent was resolved.
findings.suggestedFix: Default to no non-essential collection, consolidate/batch analytics after consent, and remove or defer third-party widgets.

findings.summary: Cookie and browser-policy posture is overly permissive.
findings.evidence: All nine observed cookies were SameSite=None and several non-auth cookies were script-readable; Referrer-Policy and Permissions-Policy were absent.
findings.suggestedFix: Use Lax/Strict unless cross-site behavior is required, add HttpOnly where JavaScript access is unnecessary, and set explicit browser policies.

findings.summary: The app-like timetable surface exposes a manifest but no demonstrated offline fallback.
findings.evidence: The timetable has a web app manifest, but navigator.serviceWorker.controller was absent in the tested load and no offline fallback was exposed.
findings.suggestedFix: Register a service worker for the timetable app shell and useful offline/retry state, while keeping server-rendered fallback content.

findings.summary: The consent choice strongly steers users toward tracking or payment.
findings.evidence: The settings screen presents a dominant Agree button for tailored ads and a CZK 49/month alternative; the non-pay, non-targeted detailed choice is a lower-emphasis text link.
findings.suggestedFix: Offer equally prominent accept, reject/non-targeted and customise choices, with neutral wording and no financial penalty framing for privacy.

findings.summary: Submitting the empty timetable form gives no visible field-specific guidance.
findings.evidence: Before/after screenshots of the empty submit are effectively unchanged and the origin/destination inputs are not marked required in DOM.
findings.suggestedFix: Declare required fields, validate after interaction, focus the first invalid field and announce concise recovery text with aria-describedby/live regions.

findings.summary: Several meaningful inputs disable or omit autofill assistance.
findings.evidence: Homepage search and timetable origin/destination use autocomplete=off; timetable email/comment fields omit useful tokens, although login correctly uses username/current-password/one-time-code.
findings.suggestedFix: Keep correct login tokens and add suitable address/email tokens where standard tokens apply; avoid autocomplete=off unless necessary.

findings.summary: Image delivery is disproportionate and poorly responsive.
findings.evidence: The homepage transferred 14.2MB across 315 image requests; 30/100 inspected images were oversized, 45 used legacy formats and 13 lacked srcset.
findings.suggestedFix: Generate AVIF/WebP responsive variants, emit srcset/sizes and lazy-load below-fold images while reserving dimensions.

findings.summary: The page performs extensive background work before user demand.
findings.evidence: A fresh load issued 480 requests, 452 to non-main origins, with video metadata, assistant and analytics traffic plus repeated long tasks.
findings.suggestedFix: Gate widgets/media on visibility or intent, deprioritise background fetches and stop idle/background work.

findings.summary: Third-party and media cost is not proportionate to the first-view portal task.
findings.evidence: 16.45MB of 16.72MB transferred came from non-main origins; scripts included assistant/analytics and the DOM contained three video players.
findings.suggestedFix: Set per-template byte/request budgets, defer embeds and media, and load analytics/widgets only when justified by consent and user value.

findings.summary: The search portal has no structured agent-facing capability surface.
findings.evidence: Discoverability is strong (92% raw/rendered coverage), but no WebMCP or agentic-tool registration was found; Lighthouse agentic-browsing scored 45.
findings.suggestedFix: For the search/timetable tasks, expose narrow, permissioned WebMCP tools with explicit parameters and safe confirmation boundaries.

findings.summary: The initial memory footprint is high for a portal landing page.
findings.evidence: The heap summary contained 1,532,409 nodes and 90.9MB self size at baseline (post interaction 1,535,702 nodes/91.2MB), including 162k closures post-interaction.
findings.suggestedFix: Virtualise/defer below-fold portal modules, release hidden widget state, and budget DOM/closure counts per module.

taskList.title: Cut the homepage request/image/widget budget and main-thread work
Repair accessible names, heading order, focus and target sizes
Make search results genuinely reflow at mobile widths
Replace the obstructive, steered consent experience with a semantic neutral choice
Deploy a complete CSP and browser security/privacy policies
Minimise analytics and third-party collection until valid consent
Reserve image/widget space and emit responsive intrinsic image metadata
Fix runtime errors, deprecated APIs, source maps and BFCache blockers
Add explicit timetable validation and offline fallback
Reduce initial DOM, closure and heap footprint
Expose narrow, permissioned agent tools for search and timetable tasks
Use View Transitions for meaningful portal state changes
